1.1: In the beginning, God brought forth the heavens and the earth.
1.2: Though the earth was unshaped and empty, and darkness veiled the deep, the Spirit of God hovered over the waters.
1.3: Then God said, 'Let there be light,' and light came forth.
1.4: And God saw the light, that it was good; and God separated the light from the darkness.
1.5: And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And evening came, then morning followed — Day One.
1.6: Then God said, 'Let there be a space between the waters, dividing the waters from the waters.'
1.7: So God made the expanse, dividing the waters below from the waters above; and it was so.
1.8: And God called the expanse Heaven. And evening came, then morning followed — Day Two.
1.9: Then God said, 'Let the waters under the heaven be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear'; and it was so.
1.10: And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters He called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
1.11: Then God said, 'Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit according to its kind.' And it was so.
1.12: The earth brought forth vegetation — plants yielding seed, and trees bearing fruit according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
1.13: And evening came, then morning followed — Day Three.
1.14: Then God said, 'Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to divide the day from the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years.'
1.15: And let them shine in the heavens to give light upon the earth'; and it was so.
1.16: Then God fashioned two great lights — the greater to rule the day, and the lesser to watch the night; and He scattered the stars as witnesses of His order.
1.17: And God set them in the heavens above, that their light might reach the earth — signs of His order shining upon creation.
1.18: And they ruled over day and night, to reveal what was light and what was dark; and God saw the harmony of His order, and called it good.
1.19: And evening came, then morning followed — the fourth day fulfilled its purpose beneath His order.
1.20: Then God spoke, and the waters swarmed with life; and the birds rose to the skies, gliding above the earth beneath heaven’s vast expanse.
1.21: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, which the waters brought forth abundantly, each after its kind, and every winged bird after its kind; and God saw that it was good.
1.22: Then God blessed them, saying, 'Be fruitful and multiply; let the seas be filled with life, and the skies echo with wings above the earth.'
1.23: And evening came, and morning followed — the fifth day rested in the grace of His order.
1.24: Then God spoke, and the earth brought forth life — beasts and creatures of every kind, great and small, each after its design; and it was so.
1.25: And God made the beasts of the earth after their kind, the cattle after their kind, and everything that creeps upon the ground after its kind; and God saw that it was good.
1.26: Then God said, “Let Us make humanity in Our image, according to Our likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the cattle, and all the earth, and over every creeping thing that moves upon the ground.”
1.27: So God created humanity in His image; in the likeness of His heart He shaped them — male and female, reflections of His communion.
1.28: God blessed them and spoke: “Flourish and multiply; fill the earth with My life, and guide it with wisdom — reign gently over all that breathes beneath the sun.”
1.29: Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant and every tree with fruit upon the earth for your nourishment.”
1.30: And to every creature that moves, I have given the green plants for food. And it was so.
1.31: And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was exceedingly good. And there was evening, and there was morning — Day Six.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
